## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sulasājātaka* (Ja 419) is a narrative included in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, opening with the verse beginning *Idam suvaṇṇakāyūran ti* ("Here is a golden necklace") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The framing story (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivers the tale concerning a clever servant-girl (*dāsī*) of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika who outwitted a robber, explaining that she had similarly demonstrated presence of mind (*ṭhānuppattikapaññā*) to slay him in a past life [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897].
Automated DharmaNexus analysis confirms strong Pali-internal text reuse between this text and the *Kuṇḍalakesātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 21, §1.1–9.4 ↔ §27.1–35.4) as well as the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0509a) and other portions of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0513a3 and Atk S0513a4) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies cross-language alignments between verses of this text and the Sanskrit *Nītiśāstra* [DharmaNexus].
